title: Inbound APIs, external IDs, and duplicate protection
summary: Accept repeated incoming data without creating duplicate business requests, while distinguishing record identity from operation identity.
prerequisites: M12 Warranty_Request__c and M15 contract design.
learningObjectives: Use an external ID for stable record matching.
Define conflicting reuse of an idempotency key.
Compare standard REST upsert with custom orchestration.

sections.heading: Understand the mechanism
body: An external ID identifies a Salesforce record using a key from another system. It lets an integration find or upsert the same record without first knowing its Salesforce Id. Upsert means create when there is no matching record and update when there is one. It is useful for synchronization, but it does not by itself make every downstream side effect exactly once.

An idempotency key identifies a business operation. The same request repeated after a timeout should return the existing result or safely continue that operation. The key must have a defined scope and payload meaning. Reusing WARRANTY-100 for a different vehicle should be a conflict, not a quiet overwrite of the original customer's request.

The starter VIN__c is a unique external ID on Vehicle__c. M12 adds a unique external Request_Key__c on Warranty_Request__c. These keys solve different matching needs: VIN identifies a vehicle; the request key identifies a particular warranty operation. A vehicle can legitimately have more than one check over time, so VIN alone is usually insufficient as the operation key.

Prefer the standard API when the requirement is ordinary record synchronization and the standard permission model fits. Use a custom endpoint or service when accepting the operation requires additional validation, state transitions, or a controlled result. In either case, authenticate the caller, limit its permissions, validate payload fields, and ensure repeated input cannot trigger an unintended duplicate external action.

callouts.text: Record identity says which entity; operation identity says which attempt at a business intention.

sections.heading: Northstar Motors worked example
body: A partner sends key WARRANTY-100 for NS-001 three times because its first two responses were lost. Northstar should have one request for that key. The second and third deliveries should not reset Succeeded to Queued or launch another provider operation without a defined reason. Now send the same key with NS-002: the service should reject conflicting reuse.

A standard upsert can demonstrate stable record matching with the existing VIN field. Use the placeholder request below only in a controlled authenticated API tool, replacing the host and version for your training org. Unit tests can instead exercise the application service directly without requiring any external client or server.

callouts.text: Why should an update of a matching vehicle not automatically count as a new warranty request?

sections.heading: Build and inspect
body: Use the declared unique external IDs. If storing a normalized request fingerprint, add Payload_Fingerprint__c Text(64) to Warranty_Request__c explicitly and document the canonical fields included; it is not already in the starter.

steps.title: Define identity and conflict rules
steps.instruction: State the record key, operation key, key scope, fields that must match on a repeat, and behavior after success or failure.
steps.expected: A repeated key has an unambiguous response.

steps.title: Implement the acceptance boundary
steps.instruction: Validate allowed inputs, find or create the request under a durable uniqueness constraint, and preserve terminal results on a legitimate repeat.
steps.expected: Three deliveries correspond to one business request.

steps.title: Test repetition and disagreement
steps.instruction: Submit identical input three times, then reuse the key with a different vehicle. Add a concurrency analysis explaining why query-before-insert alone is insufficient.
steps.expected: Identical repeats are safe; conflicting reuse is rejected.

sections.heading: Failure cases and boundaries
body: An external-ID field that is not unique can still allow ambiguous matching or duplicates under some operations. State the uniqueness requirement explicitly for the exercise.
Upserting a record can fire automation again. Check that the automation responds to meaningful changes or operation identity rather than treating every write as a new external action.

callouts.text: Do not promise exactly-once effects merely because an endpoint uses upsert.

exercise.title: Accept one request three times
exercise.brief: Build and verify a stable inbound request contract with conflict handling.
steps: Test repeat delivery and terminal-state preservation.
Reject changed payload under the same key.
acceptance: One request exists for three identical deliveries.
A successful request is not silently restarted.
Conflicting key reuse returns an explicit error.
exercise.stretch: Explain one limitation and propose a small follow-up experiment before extending the implementation.

knowledgeCheck.question: What does upsert guarantee conceptually?
knowledgeCheck.answer: It chooses create or update based on matching record identity; downstream behavior still requires design.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why not use VIN as every request key?
knowledgeCheck.answer: The same vehicle can have distinct legitimate checks at different times.

knowledgeCheck.question: What must a repeat compare?
knowledgeCheck.answer: The normalized fields that define the original operation, so conflicting reuse cannot overwrite its meaning.

recap: Separate entity identity from operation identity.
